what.label: What We Do
what.title: Practical skills. Real income.
what.homeBody: Start with simple equipment and locally available Tanzanian ingredients — no import needed.
what.businessBody: Learn pricing, costing, machine setup and how to find your first customers and start selling.
what.brandBody: Scale production, build a brand, and position yourself for hotels, restaurants and supermarkets.
what.intro: Nelwa's Academy is a digital learning platform teaching practical ice cream production and entrepreneurship — designed for the African market, using African ingredients and real African business strategies.

courses.label: Our Courses
courses.title: From your first scoop to your first sale.
courses.subtitle: Three paths, one destination — a profitable African ice cream business.
courses.homeBody: A gentle introduction to making ice cream at home using a small machine and locally available ingredients. Perfect for families and first-timers.
courses.homePoints: Basic ice cream science|Local ingredient substitution|Simple recipes you can make tonight|Equipment basics
courses.softBody: This is the course that gets you selling — not just making. Mercy walks you through everything she learned building Nelwa's Gelato.
courses.softPoints: Ingredients & product formulation|Machine setup & daily maintenance|How to price for profit|Costing your product correctly
courses.gelatoBody: Private business consultation with Mercy Kitomari. Get your personalised roadmap for launching or scaling an ice cream brand in Africa.
courses.gelatoPoints: Launching your own gelato brand|Scaling production sustainably|Pricing strategy & margin optimisation|B2B: hotels, supermarkets, restaurants

story.label: Our Story
story.title: Built From One Machine and a Big Dream
story.p1: Mercy Nenelwa Kitomari started Nelwa's Gelato in 2012 — not in a factory or a funded startup, but at home, with a single machine making 5 litres of ice cream each night, selling it during her lunch break at the bank.
story.p2: From that one machine, she built one of Tanzania's most celebrated food brands. Featured on CNN's African Start-Up series and BBC's African Dream, Nelwa's Gelato grew from 180kg to 1,200kg of production per month — using uniquely Tanzanian flavours like mango, jackfruit, clove, cardamom, and baobab.
story.p3: Now, through Nelwa's Academy, she is sharing everything she knows — so the next generation of African entrepreneurs can build their own story.
story.quote: To equip individuals with skills that generate income.
story.milestones: Founded 2012, Dar es Salaam|First client: Southern Sun Hotel|CNN African Start-Up feature|BBC African Dream series|Trained businesses in Cameroon|Multiple entrepreneur awards
story.founderAlt: Mercy Kitomari, founder of Nelwa's Academy

values.label: Our Values
values.title: What We Stand For
values.subtitle: Every lesson, every product, every partnership is built on these four principles.
values.practicalBody: Every lesson is designed to produce a real result — not just knowledge. You leave each session with something you can use today.
values.africanBody: We teach what works here. Local ingredients, local context, local market. We don't teach European methods and hope they translate.
values.businessBody: You're not just learning to make ice cream. You're learning to build a business, price products correctly, and find real customers.
values.communityBody: From Dar es Salaam to Cameroon — empowering women and youth entrepreneurs across Africa, one scoop at a time.

testimonials.label: Student Stories
testimonials.title: What Our Students Say
testimonials.subtitle: Real results from real entrepreneurs across Tanzania and beyond.
testimonials.amina: I never thought I could start a business from my kitchen. Nelwa's Academy showed me exactly how — with products I could actually find in Kariakoo market.
testimonials.grace: The soft serve course paid for itself in the first week of selling. Mercy teaches you everything you actually need — and nothing you don't.
testimonials.fatuma: Finally a course designed for our African market — local ingredients, real pricing, real customers. I now supply two restaurants in Arusha.
